prompts.prompt: Add a readability module to textstats. New file textstats/readability.py with three functions: syllable_count(word) -> int (count the groups of vowels a, e, i, o, u, y; a silent e at the end of the word does not count; every word has at least 1), sentence_count(text) -> int (use the existing sentences()), and flesch_reading_ease(text) -> float (206.835 - 1.015 * words/sentences - 84.6 * syllables/words, rounded to 2 decimals, 0.0 for text with no words). Export the three from textstats/__init__.py, write tests for each in tests/test_readability.py, and add a short section about it to the README.

I want a command-line tool for textstats: `python3 -m textstats` with three subcommands. `count FILE` prints three lines: `words: N`, `sentences: N` and `characters: N` (the length of the file's text). `top FILE [-n N]` prints the N most common words, default 10, one `word count` pair per line. `sentences FILE` prints each sentence on its own line, numbered like `1: First sentence.`. Use argparse in a new textstats/cli.py plus a textstats/__main__.py. If the file does not exist, print a clear error and exit with code 2. Write tests for all three commands and the missing-file case.

app.js is getting messy. Please split it into three ES modules: store.js (the items and addItem / toggleItem / removeItem / clearDone, and save the list in localStorage so it survives a reload), view.js (render() and everything that touches the DOM) and app.js (just the wiring). Load app.js from index.html as a module. While you're at it, add filter buttons All / Active / Done above the list, and show how many items each filter has.

Add due dates to notes. A note gets an optional due date (YYYY-MM-DD). `notes add TEXT --due 2026-11-01` stores it, and a bad date is rejected with exit code 2. `notes list` shows the date after the text as `(due 2026-11-01)`. `notes list --overdue` shows only the open notes whose due date is before today. And a new command `notes due` lists the open notes that have a due date, soonest first. Old notes files without a due field must keep working. This touches model.py, store.py and cli.py; please add tests for all of it.

Create a small Python package named wordstat in this folder: a command-line tool (python -m wordstat FILE...) that prints the number of lines, words and characters of each file and the 10 most common words overall, with argparse, type hints, a README and pytest tests for every function. Standard library only.
